## The Twenty-sixth Amendment and the Right to Vote at 18

Passed by Congress on March 23, 1971, and ratified on July 1, 1971, the Twenty-sixth Amendment established an age-based protection for voting rights. It bars the federal and state governments from denying or limiting a U.S. citizen’s right to vote because of age if the citizen is at least 18.

The amendment also gives Congress authority to enforce this protection through appropriate legislation.
